column1: # cpe-extra.csv — component identity that Buildroot's own metadata does not give us.
# Read by scripts/compliance/cve-check.py. Three kinds of row:
#   1. CPE declared      — a cpe:2.3 string for a component Buildroot has no CPE_ID for,
#                          so it gets checked instead of counted as an unchecked gap.
#   2. CPE=NONE          — the component genuinely has no NVD presence. NOTES must say
#                          why, and how its vulnerabilities are found instead.
#   3. component added    — a COMPONENT name that is not in the Buildroot package list is
#                          ADDED to the inventory. That is how the kernel, U-Boot and the
#                          Rockchip SDK get checked at all: they are in the image but are
#                          not Buildroot packages.
# DECISION applies to CPE=NONE rows ONLY, and separates a fact from a decision:
#   no-nvd-presence (default, may be left blank) — there is nothing to query. True
#       by definition of our own code, and of Buildroot-internal scripts.
#   accepted-risk — there is something we cannot query and we are shipping it anyway.
#       Requires REVIEWED_BY and an ISO REVIEW_BY date. Past that date THE GATE FAILS.
# The component does not change on the review date; what expires is the licence to
# stop looking. Until 2026-08-23 the two cases were written identically — a NONE and a
# sentence — so a closed-source vendor blob inherited the permanence that belongs only
# to first-party code, and the file's claim of a 'quarterly review' was enforced by
# nothing. A row with a real CPE must leave these three columns empty: its findings are
# triaged per CVE in cve-triage.csv, and a second, coarser suppression path here would
# be one no CVE row ever mentions.
# MODE: gate (default — findings can block a release) or report-only (counted and listed,
#       never blocking; for components whose fix is a version rebase, not per-CVE triage).
# PAIRED WITH platform-extra.csv, WHICH IS ENFORCED. Every 'component added' row
# below is also declared in scripts/compliance/platform-extra.csv, which is what
# puts it in the SBOM. gen-sbom.sh fails unless the two sets match name for name
# and version for version, so the kernel can never again be CVE-checked here while
# being absent from the bill of materials.
# A wrong CPE is worse than a missing one: it reports a component as clean instead of
# reporting it as unchecked. Verify against the NVD CPE dictionary before adding a row
# (cve-check.py --suggest-cpe prints candidates).
# Coverage-gap closure 2026-08-12: the 19 components the report listed as NOT
# CHECKED. Every name below was resolved against the NVD CPE dictionary on
# 2026-08-12 (keyword search incl. upstream aliases: cdialog, v4l-utils, GNU
# libiconv, GNU time). Exactly one has an NVD identity — GNU nano. The NONE
# rows mean NVD has never issued an advisory under any name for the project;
# their vulnerabilities reach us through upstream releases and distro
# advisories, which the quarterly review of this file is the checkpoint for.

column1: platform
column6: Closed-source Rockchip media/ISP/NPU libraries shipped as binaries (librkaiq, rockit, librknnmrt). RISK ACCEPTED, not merely unmappable: no NVD CPE exists, no source is published, and nothing can be queried - so a clean CVE report says nothing about this code, which runs on every unit. Only librknnmrt is loaded at runtime, by the satisense-edge daemon, and it processes model tensors rather than network input; the rest is present but unreferenced. Mitigation is the reachability boundary plus watching Rockchip's release notes. REVIEW means re-reading those notes and re-confirming what is still loaded - not re-checking NVD, which will never have anything.

column1: platform
column6: Closed-source Rockchip blobs that run before U-Boot and are packed into idblock.img and download.bin per RKBOOT/RV1106MINIALL.ini (DDR init rv1106_ddr_924MHz_v1.15.bin, SPL rv1106_spl_v1.02.bin). RISK ACCEPTED: no CPE, no source, nothing queryable, and this is the earliest code on the unit - it runs before every control this programme has built, so a defect here is under all of them. Not reachable from the network or from any shipped service: it executes only between reset and U-Boot, and the flash-time usbplug blob requires physical MaskROM access. Fixes arrive only as a new rkbin drop, and a drop changes the bootloader, which the A/B updater cannot deliver - it is a reflash. REVIEW means checking Rockchip's rkbin repository for a newer RV1106 loader and deciding whether it is worth a reflash. Added 2026-08-22, when the SBOM/CVE inventory reconciliation found the bootloader blobs were in neither document.
